solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get wind about one failure of justice

indicators.note: one thing lying about another surrounds it, so the wind's letters wrap round the other piece

parts.note: the mistral is a cold northerly wind of southern France

explanation.surface: Someone hears a rumour about a single miscarriage of justice.
explanation.walkthrough: MISTRAL takes I after its fourth letter. To 'get wind' of something is to hear of it, but here wind is just the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistrial is a trial made invalid by an error, so it is a legal failure.

clue.text: Architectural feature encountered on work initially Egyptian

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so they are placed in sequence

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An Egyptian architectural detail found in an early archaeological dig.
explanation.definitionFit: A metope is the square panel between triglyphs in a Doric frieze, a feature of classical buildings.

clue.text: Covering place in swell burst of extravagance

indicators.note: covering something means going over and around it, so the swell encloses the place

parts.note: a surge is a swell of the sea
PL is the abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: Someone splashes out on covering the house in a burst of spending.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator comes first in the clue, so the solver must read it as the swell doing the covering, not the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A splurge is a lavish spending spree, a sudden outburst of extravagance.

clue.text: Characteristic behaviour of a parrot is concerning round robin

parts.note: a round robin is a petition signed by many

explanation.surface: A bird-watcher writes about parrots and robins, both birds.
explanation.walkthrough: A round robin is a petition whose signatures are arranged in a circle so no one appears to have signed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Parrots are known for copying words over and over, so saying things again is their trademark.

clue.text: Unconventional self-betrothal turning out well finally

indicators.note: something unconventional departs from the usual order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd marriage to oneself that ends happily after all.
explanation.definitionFit: All for the best is an idiom saying that something unwelcome will have a good outcome in the end.

clue.text: Something of a grain surplus with Kent being stripped

indicators.note: stripping something takes off its outer layer, so the county loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the county name without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A farming report about a grain surplus in Kent, England's garden county.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the protein found in wheat and other cereals, so it is part of a grain.

clue.text: Be the first boy swallowing ecstasy

indicators.note: a thing swallowing another takes it inside, so the boy encloses the drug

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A boy is the first to take a pill of ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead is to be in front of everyone else, first in a race or line.

clue.text: Wine, free inside, one feature of the Britannia Arms?

definitions.text: one feature of the Britannia Arms?

indicators.note: inside means the word for free goes within the wine

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine used as communion wine

explanation.surface: Wine served free inside a pub called the Britannia Arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' suggests a pub name but means what Britannia holds in her hands. Tent is an obscure Spanish red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia, the figure personifying Britain, is shown holding a three-pronged spear in her arms.

clue.text: Like some ovenware, new and freshly in stock

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: doing something freshly means doing it anew, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A shop advertises new oven dishes just arrived in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonstick pans and dishes have a coating that stops food adhering, a property of much cookware.

clue.text: Standing stone eroded front and back in ancient mount

indicators.note: wearing away both ends removes the first and last letters of the stone

parts.note: a stele is an upright carved stone slab

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds a weathered standing stone on an ancient hill.
explanation.walkthrough: STELE loses its S and final E to leave TEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tel (or tell) is an artificial mound in the Middle East built up from layers of ancient settlement.

clue.text: What could bring to fruition election in leaderless country

indicators.note: without a leader means the country loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Holding an election in a country without a leader might bring plans to fruition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollination fertilises flowers so that they set fruit, literally bringing them to fruition.

clue.text: Advance encircling Jerusalem is one that might take off

indicators.note: encircling means surrounding, so the advance goes round the following words

parts.note: an imprest is an advance of money, a loan
Sion (Zion) is the hill of Jerusalem, and a name for the city

explanation.surface: An army advance surrounds Jerusalem, as if something is about to launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests an aircraft but is British slang for mimicking. Imprest is an old word for an advance of public money.
explanation.definitionFit: An impressionist mimics famous people, and to take someone off is British slang for imitating them.

clue.text: Soldiers trapping a traitor in professional operations

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so the professional surrounds the traitor

explanation.surface: Troops catch a turncoat during a professional military operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' for a traitor is a standard crossword equivalence; the short forms of professional and operations finish it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paratroops are soldiers trained to drop by parachute, so they are a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Attend club

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as two words, ..., to be present at
second meaning: to strike or hit hard

explanation.walkthrough: Club looks like a noun, somewhere one might attend, but it is the verb meaning hit; the first sense splits the answer into BE AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at an event is to attend it, and to beat someone is to club them.

clue.text: American fellow I found in Verona travelling?

definitions.text: American fellow I found in Verona travelling?

indicators.note: found in means placed within, so the first pieces sit inside the city's letters
travelling means moving about, so the city's letters are shifted around

parts.note: cat is American jazz slang for a man, a guy

explanation.surface: An American tourist introduces himself as visiting Verona on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: an American on holiday in Italy is exactly what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacationer is the American word for a holidaymaker, someone travelling for leisure.

clue.text: Group holding record time for chamber piece

indicators.note: a thing holding another has it inside, so the group's letters go round the others

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A group of musicians holds the record time for playing a chamber work.
explanation.walkthrough: An EP is an extended-play record, longer than a single but shorter than an album.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is a composition for seven players, a standard form of chamber music.

clue.text: The Spanish sparkling wine cold is variable

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone complains that Spanish cava served cold varies in quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic means stretchable or flexible, as in 'an elastic timetable', so it can be adjusted and is variable.

clue.text: Put arms on jacket two-thirds finished in bright yellow, not large

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
only two-thirds of it is completed, so the last third of the word is missing
not large means the abbreviation for large is dropped from the colour

explanation.surface: A tailor sews a coat of arms onto a jacket, partly made in bright yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' here is heraldic arms, not limbs or weapons; the jacket keeps four of its six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To emblazon is to decorate with a heraldic device, putting a coat of arms on something.

clue.text: Vermin around mug — a potential source of disease

indicators.note: the vermin go around the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: to mug someone is to rob them

explanation.surface: Rodents found round a drinking mug could spread disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Mug looks like a cup but is the verb meaning to attack and steal from someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A microbe is a microscopic organism, and some such germs cause illness.

clue.text: Maybe Tom is about stripped for nightclub

indicators.note: about means around, so the tom goes around the other word

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A man called Tom has stripped off at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' warns that Tom is an example of something, a male cat, not a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub or restaurant offering entertainment while people eat and drink.

clue.text: Attitude of aloofness putting off girl

indicators.note: putting something off here means dropping it, so the girl's name is removed

parts.note: keeping one's distance is being aloof
Di is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A standoffish manner that puts a girl off a suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: DISTANCE loses DI from its front.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position or point of view taken on something, an attitude.

clue.text: Company in time making something new

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A firm, given time, makes an innovation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but here it is simply its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A coinage is a newly invented word or phrase, a fresh creation.

clue.text: Empty garden? Some moving in these?

definitions.text: Empty garden? Some moving in these?

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only its outer letters
moving means shifting around, so these letters change places

explanation.surface: A garden looks empty, so perhaps some little statues should be moved in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: garden ornaments that a bare garden might gain. Several solvers found the definition loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden gnomes are small ornamental figures of bearded men, placed in gardens to fill them.

clue.text: World lacking good rounded projection

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is taken away from the world

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A sour remark that the world lacks any good rounded features.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobe is a rounded part that sticks out, like an earlobe or a lobe of a leaf.

clue.text: Knocking down protest hero holding appeal

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: the hero holds the next piece within, surrounding it

parts.note: a lion is a brave hero
it means sex appeal, as in 'she's got it'

explanation.surface: A protest hero campaigns against a building being pulled down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for appeal, meaning sex appeal, is an old crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolition is the act of tearing down a building, which is knocking it down.

clue.text: Evil character, one in the past

explanation.surface: A wicked person who was once someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello, a byword for wickedness.

clue.text: Reformed Rasta or Zion believer

indicators.note: something reformed is remade in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Rastafarian who has converted, about Zion, which Rastas revere.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zoroastrian follows the ancient Persian religion of Zoroaster, so is a religious believer.

clue.text: Focus regularly seen in Taoism

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is read

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Concentration is a recurring theme in Taoist philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: To focus on something is to aim at it; as nouns both mean a target or object.

clue.text: Idea that's out Oscar introduced

indicators.note: something introduced is put into another thing, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A suggestion that Oscar Wilde was excluded from society.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes into NOT IN between its I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a concept or belief, which is an idea.

clue.text: Those gawping around king with no clothes

indicators.note: the gawpers are placed around the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: Onlookers gawp at a king who has no clothes, as in the Emperor's New Clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Starkers is British slang for stark naked, which the surface's story of a naked king plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkers is informal British for completely naked, wearing no clothes at all.
